ai.title: Windows path and script fixes
ai.summary: Updated `common/src/db/drizzle.config.ts` to use `__dirname` with backslash-to-forward-slash conversion for Windows compatibility. Modified `common/package.json` `db:start` script to use `(timeout 1 || sleep 1)` for cross-platform waiting. Added `trustedDependencies` for tree-sitter packages in root `package.json` and `@t3-oss/env-core` to `web/package.json`. Updated `schema.knowledge.md` with local development and Windows-specific path handling instructions.

eli5.text: The app now runs its database setup tools correctly on Windows computers, where file paths use backslashes instead of forward slashes that Mac and Linux use. If you use the app on Windows, the database helper that manages the app's data will now find its configuration files without errors, and the setup waits the right amount of time between steps on both Windows and other systems. These fixes are part of the current version of the app.

ai.title: Rename Manicode to Codebuff in npm-app
ai.summary: Internal rename of the CLI package and identifiers from Manicode to Codebuff across the npm-app source. Updates include command names, UI messages, file references (.codebuffignore), and npm install instructions. The entry point function and update logic were refactored to use the new name.

eli5.text: When you interact with the coding assistant in the npm-app directory, you'll now see the name 'Codebuff' everywhere instead of the previous name 'Manicode' - in welcome messages, help menus, exit messages, and update notifications. The team renamed the tool throughout its codebase, including the command used to update it and the ignore file configuration. If you were paying attention to what the assistant calls itself, you'd notice it now says 'Codebuff will read and write files...' instead of the old name.

ai.title: Version bump 1.0.100
ai.summary: Bump `codebuff` version to 1.0.100. Updates `npm-app/package.json`. Internal release increment.

eli5.text: The assistant tool you use got quietly reissued as version 1.0.100, but the version number is just a label. The actual user-noticeable gains in this release are that the referral program now caps how many referred friends each user can bring in rather than sharing one global limit, successful referral redemption once again restores your usage quota, and the database now tracks when each account was created and recomputes your plan limits based on your actual billing cycle. Additionally, the file-processing system now consistently uses only the latest copy of a file you share, making the assistant less likely to act on stale file contents, and the rebranding that replaced the old product name with Codebuff is finished across every public-facing page and message. These changes are live today

ai.title: Rename agent persona from Mani to Buffy in system prompt
ai.summary: The agent persona name in `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` changed from Mani to Buffy. This updates the intro prompt and project file tree prompt to reflect the new identity. No functional logic or API behavior changed. Only the persona name string was updated.

eli5.text: The assistant now introduces itself as Buffy instead of Mani when it starts helping with a coding project. If you watched the assistant's welcome message or its view of the project files, you would see the name Buffy where Mani used to appear. This is purely a behind-the-scenes rename with no effect on how the assistant works or what it can do.

ai.title: Decrease free credits for anon/login
ai.summary: CREDITS_USAGE_LIMITS in common/src/constants.ts reduced ANON from 1000 to 750 and FREE from 2500 to 1500. PAID limit remains 10000. Scope limited to shared core constants.

eli5.text: Your free monthly allowance of assistant uses has been cut: guest visitors now get fewer uses per month, and free sign-up users get fewer as well, while paying users keep their higher limit. If you used this product without paying, you'll hit your monthly cap sooner than before and be asked to upgrade or wait. The change is already in effect for everyone on the free tiers.

ai.title: Extract testimonials into separate data file
ai.summary: Moved hardcoded testimonial objects from `web/src/app/page.tsx` to new `web/src/lib/testimonials.ts`. Defines `Testimonial` type and exports `testimonials` array. `page.tsx` imports the array to render the Marquee component. No functional changes to UI.

eli5.text: The team moved the customer quotes that appear on the homepage into a single, dedicated container used only for storing that kind of text, while the page that displays them now simply reads from it. You would not see the quotes change or move on the site, but if someone opened the storage container they would find a tidy list of the three quotes ready to be shown. A new optional slot for a picture was also added to each quote entry, though the homepage has not been updated to use it yet, so the slot sits empty and invisible for now.

ai.title: Add optional avatar field to testimonials
ai.summary: Testimonial type gains optional `avatar` string field. `web/src/lib/testimonials.ts` populates `avatar` paths for Sarah Chen, Michael Park, Alex Rivera. `web/src/app/page.tsx` renders `img` element conditionally when `avatar` present, styled `w-8 h-8 rounded-full object-cover`.

eli5.text: When you read a testimonial on the website, you'll now see a small circular photo of the person next to their name and job title, instead of just their text. The website was updated to show these profile pictures for three specific testimonials (Sarah Chen, Michael Park, and Alex Rivera), pulling each photo from a dedicated image file. You can notice this right away by visiting the page that displays these customer quotes.

ai.title: Add Marquee testimonials to Web landing page
ai.summary: New `web/src/components/ui/marquee.tsx` added. `web/src/app/page.tsx` renders testimonial cards inside Marquee. `web/tailwind.config.ts` extended with marquee keyframes/animations. Scope: Web landing page only.

eli5.text: Visitors to the web landing page will now see a horizontally scrolling section titled "What Developers Are Saying" featuring rotating testimonial cards with quotes and developer names. The testimonials pause automatically when a visitor hovers their mouse over them, allowing time to read each quote before the scrolling resumes.

ai.title: Marquee testimonials on landing page
ai.summary: Landing page adds scrolling testimonial marquee. `testimonials.ts` type changes to `Testimonial[][]` with required `link` field. `page.tsx` renders alternating `Marquee` rows with clickable cards. New avatar and proof images added to `web/public/testimonials/`.

eli5.text: When you visit the company's main website page, you'll now see a section called "What Developers Are Saying" featuring a scrolling reel of customer quotes. Each quote appears on a clickable card that takes you to proof of what the customer said, and the cards scroll sideways in looping rows, some moving right and others left. The company added photos of the people quoted and screenshots as evidence, and updated the website's structure to make this scrolling display work.

ai.title: Fix web build errors in page.tsx and tailwind.config.ts
ai.summary: Resolved build failures in `web/src/app/page.tsx` and `web/tailwind.config.ts`. Updated JSX text nodes to use `"` entity and removed invalid quotes around `{testimonial.quote}`. Normalized `tailwind.config.ts` formatting and fixed `container.center` boolean type.

eli5.text: The website's home page had two small mistakes that stopped it from building correctly. First, the page tried to show customer quotes inside quotation marks directly in the design, which broke how text is written. Second, the design settings file had quotes around a word that was meant to be a simple yes/no choice. Both are now fixed, so the homepage displays testimonials and layout settings without any errors.

ai.title: Redeem page command text corrected to codebuff
ai.summary: Referrals redeem page command text updated from manicode to codebuff. Fixes stale branding in the copy-to-clipboard input. Scope limited to web/src/app/referrals/[code]/page.tsx. No migration or config changes required.

eli5.text: The text shown next to the "copy to clipboard" box on the referral redemption page now says "codebuff" instead of "manicode." Visitors who paste that command into their terminal to run the tool will now have the correct, up-to-date name, since the old name was leftover from a previous brand name. This fix is live today.

If you were watching the assistant work on code changes, you'd notice it now uses special file commands that keep everything linked together, making it harder for edits to get lost or confused. This only affects how the assistant handles file operations internally, so most people wouldn't see anything different.

ai.title: Fix stale edited files in system prompt
ai.summary: Edited files now appear in `getFileVersionUpdates` even when absent from `previousFilePaths`. `updatedFiles` merges `previousFilePaths` and `editedFilePaths` before content diffing, removing the separate `editedUnreadFilePaths` set. `addedFiles` simplifies to `updatedFiles` plus `newFiles`. Scope limited to `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`.

eli5.text: When you edit a file during a coding task, the assistant now reliably remembers to include your latest changes when it checks which files need updating. Previously, edited files could be missed if they weren't already tracked, causing the assistant to work with outdated content. This fix ensures edited files are always considered alongside previously known files, so you won't encounter situations where your recent edits get ignored.

ai.summary: Version string in npm-app/package.json incremented from 1.0.100 to 1.0.101. No functional code changes; package metadata update only.

Updating gets you the newer assistant name in the system prompt, lower free credits for anonymous or logged-in users, and testimonials pulled from a separate file (with optional avatars). You'd also see the new scrolling testimonial marquee on the landing page, the corrected 'codebuff' referral text, and a fix so already-edited files show up correctly after updates. These changes are live now.
